speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble feeding and your belly looks swollen. To help me understand what is wrong, can you tell me when these symptoms first started and if you are vomiting anything you eat?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the update; the worsening pain with touch and distension are concerning. Does the baby pass gas or stool, and have you noticed any specific sounds like high-pitched gurgling or a complete lack of bowel movements? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray

text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Patient
text:
The abdomen still looks swollen and the baby seems uncomfortable, especially in the lower abdomen.

speaker: Doctor
text: The discomfort localized to the lower abdomen is a key finding. Does the baby pass stool that looks like "currant jelly" or has there been any vomiting? REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_Ultrasound; REQUEST IMAGES

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: No "currant jelly" stool observed; no vomiting reported. Ultrasound performed: Target sign identified in the mid-abdomen consistent with intussusception.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception. The clinical picture of abdominal distension, tenderness, and the ultrasound finding of a "target sign" in an 8-month-old boy confirms this diagnosis.
